claims.text: Tailored annealing temperatures can direct phase evolution in Al–Co–Cr–Fe–Ni high-entropy alloys.
Regulated cooling rates can direct phase evolution in Al–Co–Cr–Fe–Ni high-entropy alloys.
Controlled thermal treatments can selectively stabilize desired phase constituents in Al–Co–Cr–Fe–Ni high-entropy alloys.
The as-cast Al–Co–Cr–Fe–Ni alloy has a mixed-phase microstructure.
An inert processing atmosphere avoids oxidation during heat treatment.
Annealing temperature and cooling rate modify nucleation and growth kinetics.
Nucleation and growth kinetics govern the formation and distribution of FCC and BCC crystalline phases.
Tailored thermal processing alters the energy landscape of the alloy.
Tailored thermal processing alters diffusion kinetics in the alloy.
Changes in the energy landscape and diffusion kinetics enable controlled nucleation and growth of targeted phases.
Tailored thermal processing can suppress unwanted intermetallic phases.
Controlled heat treatment will increase the fraction of a targeted FCC or BCC phase relative to the untreated state.
Controlled heat treatment will reduce deleterious secondary phases relative to the untreated state.
The proposed control of phase evolution is effective within moderate ranges of annealing temperature and cooling rate.
Extreme annealing temperatures or cooling rates may cause unexpected phase formation or degrade microstructural quality.
